The Owls were pegged by sportsbooks, modelers, and pundits as one of the worst teams in the country, but they defied all of those predictions with a 10-win season that culminated with them defeating Jacksonville State in the Conference USA Championship Game. Unfortunately, all that success meant the sharks were circling, and Kennesaw State lost several key players to the transfer portal this offseason. Thus, it's no surprise that the Owls have sputtered to a 1-4 start in 2026. That said, they should have a decent chance to build some momentum against Missouri State on Wednesday night. Kennesaw State is a 3-point favorite on the road. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET on CBSSN from Robert W. Plaster Stadium in Springfield, Missouri. Both squads enter Week 7 sitting at 1-4 and stinging from recent defeats. The Bears are regrouping after a decisive 34-13 road loss to Western Kentucky, while the Owls hope to rebound from a heartbreaking 27-26 defeat at the hands of Jacksonville State. My Kennesaw State vs Missouri State prediction weighs the rushing matchup against two offenses looking for a more complete performance. The win prices and a separate total pick follow. Kennesaw State vs Missouri State Prediction Kennesaw State moneyline (58¢ on Kalshi ) My Kennesaw State vs Missouri State prediction centers on the Owls' rushing attack against a vulnerable Missouri State front. The Owls average 376.4 total yards per game with a rushing attack churning out 157.0 yards at a healthy 4.73 per carry. Missouri State is the wrong opponent for that. The Bears surrender 449.6 total yards and 32.4 points per game, and they get gashed on the ground specifically, allowing 196.4 rushing yards at 4.77 per carry. Rickie Collins is the engine for Kennesaw State. He has passed for 1,042 yards while adding 246 rushing yards and four touchdowns, giving the Owls a quarterback who can extend drives with his legs when the pocket breaks down. He has help behind him too. Boogie Woods III and Latrelle Murrell combine to average 5.2 yards a carry, which is exactly the profile you want against a front allowing almost 200 rushing yards per game. Kennesaw State has scored just 22.6 points per game, but its last two losses came by one and three points. Against this defense, I like the Owls to turn another competitive game into a win. picks.blurb: The Kennesaw State Owls (1-4, 0-1 CUSA) won this league last year and were expected to contend for the title again, but they've had a disappointing start to the year and have dropped back-to-back one-score games. Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. Last week, they lost to a Western Kentucky game that looked like it could be the worst in the conference. If you are looking for some betting advice for the matchup, we've got you covered. Still, he's the driving force behind this offense considering he also leads the way in a quarterback-centric rushing attack. That offense is a strength relative to the defense, which has been pretty rough overall, particularly against the pass. Missouri State's offense has its own issues, though, and it benched quarterback Skyler Locklear for Henry Belin IV last week. picks.headline: Ohio State On SI Staff Picks: Can Buckeyes Get Revenge on Indiana in Week 7?
picks.blurb: Ohio State On SI Staff Picks: Can Buckeyes Get Revenge on Indiana in Week 7? Skip to main content SI.COM 2025 Football Bracket Buckeyes In the NFL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES BB This game needs no introduction. Some may argue this is the game Ohio State has been preparing fo r all season long . Now it has a chance to go to Indiana and rewrite a wrong from last December, when it lost the Big Ten Championship game to the Hoosiers, which ultimately led to them completing their undefeated season. Ohio State isn’t undefeated like Indiana is. However, the Buckeyes are rolling through the start of the Big Ten schedule without any real hiccups. Ohio State (5-1, 3-0 Big Ten) has had this game against the Hoosiers (6-0, 3-0 Big Ten) earmarked on the schedule since it was released. So much so that both teams have remained the class of the Big Ten all year long, with a possible elimination scenario in play come December, ahead of the Big Ten title game in Indianapolis. Someone’s supremacy must be disrupted . Will the Buckeyes struggle again, or will the Hoosiers exploit their weaknesses? Check out our staff picks as the game gets underway. Ohio State vs. Indiana Week 7 Outlook Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day watches during the NCAA football game against the Maryland Terrapins at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Oct. 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: noon ET/9 a.m. PT TV Channel: FOX (consult TV Guide or preferred streaming provider for details). Odds: Ohio State -3; over/under is 50.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Location : Memorial Stadium – Bloomington, Ind. Ohio State’s record under Ryan Day : 87-13 (8-6 in postseason bowl games/CFP). Last time vs. Indiana: A 13-10 loss in the Big Ten title game in a top-two showdown. Ohio State leads the series dating back to 1989, 31-1-1. Pregame festivities: Big Noon Kickoff will be there. Ohio State so far this season: 5-1 (3-0 Big Ten) Zain Bando: 6-0 Dylan Buganski : 5-1 Rafael Zamorano : 4-1 (no pick in Week 6 nor Week 7) Chip Minnich : 4-0 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 28, Indiana 24 There is no such thing as a one-game season, but the Buckeyes may beg to differ. Indiana handed Ohio State one of its two back-to-back losses to end last season and now, on a fall Saturday in Bloomington, the entire year could come down to whether Ohio State can finally sneak up and regain head-to-head dominance and steal a road win. If wideout Jeremiah Smith gets space and gets comfortable thanks to Julian Sayin, and forces the defense to tire Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover, the game could easily deliver a fantastic finish in the closing minutes. We’ll see if the Buckeyes can make it interesting, or better yet, secure a road win that could change the season for good. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 31, Indiana 28 The highly anticipated, top-five Big Ten showdown between the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday hinges on how Ryan Day's squad handles sudden depth issues against an elite Indiana defense. Ohio State faces an uphill battle following a troubling availability report ruling out two of the team's most relied-upon members on offense ~ Austin Siereveld and Ja'Kobi Jackson. With Austin Siereveld missing his second straight game, the loss of the Preseason All-Big Ten selection strips the Buckeyes of their offensive line leader. This forces Gabe VanSickle and right tackle Phillip Daniels into hyper-extended roles against a vicious Hoosier pass rush; Daniels has not played since the loss at Texas on September 12th. Ja'Kobi Jackson, the team's powerhouse short-yardage back and touchdown leader (6 TDs), is sidelined with a surprise ankle injury. While Bo Jackson will shoulder the primary workload, Ja'Kobi Jackson's absence eliminates the physical lightning-and-thunder dynamic Ohio State uses to control the tempo. Could Isaiah West, who missed a key block that led to a pick-six interception in last week's Maryland game, get a chance at redemption? West offers a physical style of play comparable to Ja'Kobi Jackson. The fans who have been clamoring for Legend Bey may see Bey as a larger part of the offensive game plan. Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith will need to be creative in the run game and involve other receiving talents beyond Jeremiah Smith. With a depleted ground game and a reshuffled protection unit, the entire game plan in my estimation rests on the shoulders of junior quarterback Julian Sayin. Sayin has been using his legs to gain positive yardage in recent games and may need to run more frequently than desired by Sayin or the Ohio State coaching staff. The Ohio State defense is going to be tested, as Indiana boasts talented wide receivers in Nick Marsh and Charlie Becker, plus a strong running game led by Turbo Richard. Quarterback Josh Hoover has not yet thrown an interception this season, so perhaps Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia will be able to scheme some situations that result in a turnover. Expect a classic, physical Big Ten chess match. While Indiana enters the match healthier and with a strong defensive front, Sayin's elite talent and postseason poise will provide just enough explosive plays in a late two-minute drill to secure a tight, field-goal victory for the Buckeyes in Bloomington. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, Indiana 17 There may not be a matchup this team as well as fans circled coming into this season then the rematch of last year’s Big Ten Championship game in what may be Indiana’s biggest home game in program history. There are old and new faces on both sides, and the clash between head coaches Ryan Day and Curt Cignetti may become one of the conference’s greatest rivalries going forward. Ohio State comes into this matchup battle-tested, seeing ranked teams Iowa and Texas on the road and finishing 1-1 in those matchups. This will be Indiana’s first ranked matchup of the season, but they had a comeback victory at Nebraska last week, in which the Cornhuskers should probably have been a ranked team. This matchup will come down to how dominant Indiana can be at the line of scrimmage, as that may be the only position where Indiana may have more talent than the Buckeyes, other than maybe running back. Indiana should be able to run the ball decently and stop the run on the other side. At the end of the day, the secondary for Ohio State should limit the passing game from exploding and another weapon in the passing game has a big game next to Smith, inching Ohio State to a win in this matchup and moving what we may call in 10 years the “Cignetti-Day War” to a 2-1 Buckeye lead. Ohio State vs. Indiana predictions from our Buckeyes Wire writers
picks.blurb: Ohio State vs. Indiana predictions from our Buckeyes Wire writers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Football Toolkit Texans vs. Jags updates Caminero, Rays' bats wake up CFB winners and losers Williams takes over in G1 Ohio State vs. Indiana predictions from our Buckeyes Wire writers Phil Harrison, Buckeyes Wire Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:16 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There's a game that's been circled on the Big Ten calendar since the offseason, and it's almost here. The Indiana Hoosiers took down the Ohio State Buckeyes in the Big Ten Championship game last year in a classic, then went on to win the College Football Playoff national championship. Now, it's time for the rematch, and it takes place in Bloomington, where the Buckeyes will have to try to get things done in hostile territory. The winner will be the favorite to win the Big Ten, while the loser will have some work to do. It should be a close one, and Vegas agrees, with Ohio State listed as a very modest favorite . Before each Ohio State football game, we like to ask our writers to go out on a limb and predict the outcome of the game, and with such a huge one on the doorstep, opinions vary on this one. Here is what our writers at Buckeyes Wire predict will happen between Ohio State and Indiana on Saturday. Ohio State vs. Indiana, according to Phil Harrison, Lead Writer/Editor One game can be an exception, but two is a pattern. This isn't the same Indiana team we saw last year. We watched the Hoosiers struggle against Northwestern and Nebraska , the only teams with a pulse Curt Cignetti's crew has played. The offense hasn't been as dynamic, and the defense isn't creating the negative plays at the rate it did last season. The Buckeyes will not run all over Indiana on the ground, but they will have plenty of success through the air, just enough to pull out a huge victory. Score Prediction: Ohio State 27, Indiana 24 Ohio State vs. Indiana, according to Mark Russell, Featured Writer Ohio State gets a shot at redemption when it goes to Indiana for a rematch of the Big Ten Championship from a year ago. But these are two different teams. The Buckeyes are facing some injury issues, the most concerning of which is offensive lineman Austin Sierveld. Ohio State has struggled a bit to protect quarterback Julian Sayin, while the Hoosiers' pass rush is the best in the Big Ten. But if the line can keep Sayin clean, he should have time to carve up a suspect Indiana secondary. It'll be a tough environment, but the Buckeyes get a score late to seal the victory. Score Prediction: Ohio State 27, Indiana 17 Ohio State vs. Indiana, according to Alec Lasley, Featured Writer I fully anticipate OSU will try to get out of the gates hot, something Indiana has dealt with on its own at times this season: slow starts. If Ohio State can't get going early, it's going to put a lot of pressure on the Sayin-Smith connection, and that's when IU's defense will excel. It's going to be a close one, but I think Indiana playing at home and having the come-from-behind experience of last week under its belt will be a huge positive variable. Hoosiers start strong, finish stronger, and limit some of the explosive plays the Buckeyes typically get. Coming off a loss, Texas is eager to get back in the conference title picture with a good showing against the reeling Gators. Here's what you need to know heading into the matchup as The Big Lead locks in our final prediction for this Week 7 college football clash. Texas offensive inconsistency and defensive strength Arch Manning has shown flashes but has been uneven against better competition, with turnovers becoming a recurring issue. Pass protection has been mixed despite solid grades in some metrics, and the run game has lacked consistent explosiveness. Where Texas separates itself is on defense. The unit ranks among the better groups nationally in yards allowed and has been especially effective limiting yards after contact. Rushing off the edges and overall tackling efficiency have been strengths. That could create some real problems for a Florida offense that has looked worn down. Defensive collapse, run game issues at Florida NCAA Football: Mississippi at Florida Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Even during the Gators' win streak, critics sounded the alarm about this defense. The two-game skid has confirmed those worries. Missed tackles and coverage breakdowns have piled up? The total damage? Florida is the SEC's worst defense in total output, explosive plays allowed, and against the pass. It's the second-worst in scoring. On offense, the Florida run game that once looked dominant has been largely shut down by better fronts. Jadan Baugh's production has dropped sharply. After rushing for over 130 yards in four wins, his totals fell to 13 and then 59 yards in two losses. Questions also linger about quarterback availability with Aaron Philo listed as questionable. A potential shift to Tramell Jones Jr. would add even more uncertainty against a Texas defense that flies to the ball. Key matchup dynamics to watch Texas holds clear edges in defensive structure and home-field stability. Florida's ability to create explosive plays through play-action and yards after catch remains a theoretical strength, but recent film shows those opportunities drying up against disciplined units. Scheme-wise, Texas' ability to limit perimeter runs and finish tackles aligns poorly with what Florida has relied on. Manning should face less pressure than he did against Oklahoma, giving him cleaner looks against a secondary that has been vulnerable. Florida vs. Texas prediction: Who wins and why? Texas is the more complete team right now, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Even with offensive questions, the Longhorns' ability to control the line of scrimmage and force Florida into obvious passing situations should decide the game. Florida has the talent to keep stretches competitive, but the recent defensive regression and limited run game make a full road upset unlikely. The Big Lead Prediction: Texas 31, Florida 17

But a victory would right the ship for the Longhorns, especially if beleaguered quarterback Arch Manning and an error-prone special teams can trim the mistakes and play a clean game. Under first-year coach Jon Sumrall and breakout running back Jadan Baugh , Florida became one of the early-season darlings of college football after knocking off Ole Miss and climbing into the top 10 of the AP rankings. But the Gators have fallen out of the poll following two straight losses, and a porous Florida defense has given up a combined 83 points over the past two weeks to Missouri and South Carolina. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Florida Gators. No. 7 Texas (4-1, 1-1 SEC) vs. Florida (4-2, 2-2) When: 11 a.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: Finally, football weather. He's thrown for 1,341 yards on 70.5% passing with nine touchdowns and three interceptions and has added 104 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. The Florida Gators are in a rough spot at 4-2 as they head to Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon. After two blowout losses to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks on homecoming, Jon Sumrall 's team is in a tough spot. They were at one point being talked about as potentially being the 2019 LSU Tigers from on the precipice of collapsing. It's his first year at the helm, and the talent level still isn't quite there yet. For the Longhorns, they have beaten Ohio State, but are coming off a tough loss in the Red River Rivalry to the Oklahoma Sooners. They are in an interesting spot right now, and a win is a must for both teams. Who will get the win? Our experts made their predictions. Texas 38, Florida 24 Can we trust the Florida Gators? Honestly, no, and that includes the four-game winning streak to start the season with a massive blowout win over Ole Miss. The defense is struggling to generate pressure and the coverage on the back end has been incredibly inconsistent. Even with Texas having lost Red River last week, their success so far this season and offensive talent gets the Longhorns the win. Can the Gators get the win? Absolutely! Will they? I doubt it. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Texas 33, Florida 19 Both teams come in off dismal losses to unranked teams. The Longhorns, who haven't looked dominant this year by any means, gagged away a game they should have won against Oklahoma but for a pick six and a punt block touchdown. Florida got mollywhopped by South Carolina one game after getting throttled by Missouri. As such, it's tough to tell up from down with these two teams. But my mind immediately goes to two things. First, the Horns' front is still nasty, and Florida suddenly can't find any space for Jadan Baugh and the ground game. On the other side, Florida's defense has become a sieve, and I don't trust they've found a way to fix it yet. Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo are too much for the Longhorns, who win comfortably in Austin. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Texas 31, Florida 20 Arch Manning has faced plenty of criticism for his inconsistency this season, but this is the type of matchup that could help him get back on track. Florida's pass defense has been a major weakness, and I expect Manning to take full advantage by delivering his best performance of the 2026 season. The Longhorns have the talent to exploit the Gators' struggling secondary, and Manning should find plenty of opportunities to push the ball downfield and put points on the board. After an uneven stretch offensively, this could be the breakthrough performance Texas needs. Florida should have some success early, particularly with running back Jadan Baugh leading the way. Baugh has been one of the Gators' most productive playmakers, and I expect him to help Florida move the ball and keep the game competitive in the first half. However, Texas has the defensive talent to make adjustments and limit Florida's offensive production as the game progresses. The Gators have struggled to maintain consistency in recent weeks, and that issue will catch up with them again in Austin. Texas pulls away in the second half, with Manning and the offense doing enough to secure a much-needed win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Texas 21, Florida 17 The Gators have fallen off a bit in the last few weeks after starting red hot. Texas is coming off a disappointing loss to Oklahoma. So, you know, Steve Sarkisian is going to be looking to get his team rolling again. Last week probably showed Texas what they should be doing more often on offense. They need to run more quick-game stuff with Arch Manning, because the long, developing routes downfield aren't helping the offense. Their offensive line isn't great, so they need to start running more quick-game plays. I think this past game showed some of that, and Texas still gets the win despite the offense struggling against a decent Florida defense. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Texas 30, Florida 20 As high as I was on the Florida Gators after the Ole Miss win, that hype has come crashing down after games against Missouri and South Carolina. The offense, led by Jadan Baugh, simply hasn't looked the same, and now the availability of starting QB Aaron Philo is in question. As for Texas, the Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing loss of their own after losing Red River to a bad OU team, and they aim to get back on track. Florida's defense has been bad, to say the least, and this game may serve as a great game for Arch Manning nd Texas. Give me the Longhorns here. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Texas 28, Florida 17 Texas and Florida both need wins this week, and the pressure is even higher for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Two losses for Texas at this point in the season would make things very uncomfortable in Austin, and perhaps it would mark the beginning of the end for some important names there. I don't think that's going to happen, though. I think Texas bounces back this week behind a strong defensive performance and looks the part against Florida. If the Longhorns can limit Jaden Baugh, they'll defend home field without much issue. I think Florida hangs around, but the Longhorns put it away in the fourth quarter. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Texas It shouldn't be much of a surprise that none of our experts have picked the Gators, as they have lost our trust after the disastrous performances of the last two weeks. A win here would do wonders to get them back in our good graces. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Pete Fiutak Wed, October 14, 2026 at 6:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just a few weeks ago, Florida was coming off a 52-28 obliteration of a terrific Ole Miss team, and everything was wonderful. The Gators appeared good enough in the first season under Jon Sumrall to be in the SEC and College Football Playoff mix, the offense was unstoppable, and then a funny thing happened. The SEC figured it out. Missouri and South Carolina beat Florida by a combined score of 83-36, and now, with the schedule ahead, the 4-2 team might have to fight just to get to a bowl game. Last week at this time, Texas was No. 1, it was about to play a punchless Oklahoma team, and then a funny thing happened. The Sooners came up with creative and clutch ways to pull off a 27-24 Red River Rivalry win. The season is hardly over for the Longhorns, but now there's little margin for error over a tough second half. Florida vs Texas: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for Florida after this, with a week off before dealing with Georgia, followed up by Oklahoma, and then a trip to Kentucky. Texas starts a run of three straight home games, getting Ole Miss next and Mississippi State to follow. How is this only the sixth game between these two? Texas is 3-1-1, with the 7-7 tie coming in the first meeting in 1924. How To Watch Florida vs Texas Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ABC Location: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin, TX – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Florida Will Win The defense isn't getting fixed over the next few weeks, but that's part of what a rebuild is all about. The Gators win when the offense rocks, and the yards and points allowed are simply the cost of doing business. However, there's one key element to the Florida D that should show up huge. The pass rush is outstanding. The Gator defensive front averages close to three sacks and seven tackles for loss per game, and as good as Arch Manning is – seriously, he's really good, despite the popular opinions at the moment after the OU loss – he's still not amazing when he's getting rushed. The Texas offensive line has been better than last year for the ground game, but the pass protection has been a problem. Why Texas Will Win The Texas defense is going to stuff the Florida offense cold. Missouri and South Carolina never let Gator star Jadan Baugh and the running game breathe. The Gamecocks and Tigers combined for 18 tackles for loss against the Florida attack, and both allowed fewer than 400 yards of total offense. For all the problems in the meltdown against Oklahoma, the Texas defense was great. It allowed only 238 yards of Sooner offense, and for the fourth game in a row – including against Ohio State and Tennessee – the defense allowed fewer than 100 rushing yards. Florida vs Texas Prediction, Betting Lines It turned out to be one of the most important games of the 2025 season. Florida finished the year 4-8, but one of those wins was a 29-21 thriller over Texas. The Longhorns lost on the road to both Ohio State and Georgia – no shame there against two teams that finished with 12 wins – but that loss to the Gators kept them out of the College Football Playoff. Yeah, Texas lost to Oklahoma, but weird things happen in the Red River Rivalry. Against Florida, the offense will keep it conservative, but Arch will connect on a few deep shots to push ahead. The defense will take care of the rest. away.headline: Florida football QB Aaron Philo’s injury status gets update from Jon Sumrall
away.blurb: Philo, who is dealing with a shoulder injury, underwent warmups and was reportedly available in an emergency capacity in the 27-24 victory over Texas. "The beautiful thing is, like I said earlier, I believe we can win football games with Aaron Philo," Sumrall said. "I believe we can win football games with Tramell Jones, and those guys support each other at an elite level. But so Philo, we'll see. Like we're going to bring him back more as time is right for his return to play." For a third straight week, wide receiver Vernell Brown III did not play. However, he participated in warmups and dressed out, but did not step on the field. "He looked right at times this week late in the week, but not consistent enough for us to be like, hey, let's go put him out there," Sumrall said "So he's still not ready for maybe game action. I feel really good about where he is going into a bye week and then having a game out of that. I feel really positive about where he is, the prognosis of him playing that next week. So we'll see. But the thing I want to make abundantly clear is he's trying like crazy to get back." away.headline: Florida injury report: Philo, Brown, Stockton game-time decisions
away.blurb: Running back Duke Clark remains out and will not be available to play. Quarterback Aaron Philo and wide receivers Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton are all listed as game-time decisions ahead of the noon ET kickoff. Philo's status has been one of the biggest questions of the week. CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reported Wednesday that he had been limited in practice as he recovered from a shoulder injury. Presumably, it occurred on a fourth-quarter scramble against South Carolina last Saturday, after which he was pulled for a play and eventually the game. Stockton's appearance on the availability report is for an undisclosed reason, but he recently sustained a back injury on a targeted hit against Ole Miss. He was listed as questionable ahead of the Missouri game but ended up playing in that road loss as well as the homecoming defeat against South Carolina. Texas has two players listed on the final report, with wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman both ruled out. Defensive lineman Justus Terry and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman, who appeared on earlier versions of the report, are no longer listed. QB Aaron Philo – game-time decision WR Vernell Brown III – game-time decision WR Bailey Stockton – game-time decision Questionable (50% chance to play) Clark suffered a left ankle injury in the first half against South Carolina last Saturday and wore a boot on the sideline in the second half. His injury will likely take multiple weeks to heal. On3's Pete Nakos reported Friday that Florida is expected to start Tramell Jones against Texas, although a final determination on the quarterback situation was expected Saturday morning. Brown's absence would continue a lengthy stretch on the sideline after he sustained a knee strain against Ole Miss in Week 4. The sophomore standout missed most of that game and both of the past two contests against Missouri and South Carolina. "VB's trying to play. He's not like, 'I'm going to take the week off' or 'I'm going to take next week.' No, he's trying like hell to play," Florida head coach Jon Sumrall said Monday. "But at the same time, we have to be smart-tough, not dumb-tough." With the quarterback situation in flux due to Kamario Taylor's apparent turf toe injury sustained against Alabama, State enters the week as two touchdown underdogs on the first fall-like Saturday of football season. Coaches on both sides have a fair amount of familiarity with each other having worked together in Oxford from 2020-21 as boss and apprentice. If Lebby finds a way to get Taylor healthy and ready to roll on Saturday, this may be a barn burner inside Tiger Stadium based on the talent at the offensive skill positions for each team. Mississippi State enters the weeked ranked No. 16 nationally, according to the Week 7 AP Top 25 poll. With an extra week to lick its wounds and recover from a double-digit loss to Alabama, there's a possibility the Bulldogs can find a way to pull off a stunner and keep LSU out of the College Football Playoff entirely in Year 1 under Kiffin. The Bulldogs come in at No. 11 in the SEC, and No. 27 in ESPN's Football Power Index poll with a projected overall record of 8-4 following a 4-1 start on the season. It's interesting, because he's running a little of his old defense and he's running (Pete) Golding's defense this year. Now, he's even more multiple." Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB After LSU traveled to Lexington last weekend, Lane Kiffin and the Tigers are coming off of a disappointing loss, heading into the Week 7 matchup against Mississippi State . LSU heads into the matchup with a recent loss, while the Bulldogs are also traveling to Baton Rouge after a loss to the Crimson Tide in Week 5. Before the No. 22 LSU Tigers host the No. 16 Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday, the LSU On SI team predicts which team will win and why. Oct 3, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers safety Tamarcus Cooley (0) intercepts a pass from McNeese Cowboys quarterback Jake Strong (not pictured) during the first half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ross Abboud The time for sloppiness is over, and everyone in LSU’s football program knows it. Ole Miss was a game you could’ve won. Kentucky was a game you should never have lost. That will be LSU’s wake-up call. LSU 48, Mississippi State 24 Brooke Benedict Unlike last weekend's loss to Kentucky, LSU has to get both sides of the ball to play all four quarters, with the defense able to shut down Mississippi State's pass threat, and Sam Leavitt and his receiver options are able to make key plays during possessions. Without any system errors from the offense, defense and special teams, the team will see some much-needed success back at home, being able to win over the Bulldogs and win back their top-ranked reputation. LSU 33, Mississippi State 21 If Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor plays: Kamario Taylor has an incredible ability to control the long ball, which will force LSU's defense to account for that threat almost all of the time, and following the loss to Kentucky, I expect LSU to play a lot more tight man coverage. The LSU offense, clearly more comfortable playing at home, will establish the run with Dilin Jones against the MSST 3-3-5 defense, and LSU will win a close one late in the 4th. LSU 38, Mississippi State 31 If Taylor doesn't play: If Taylor is unavailable in Saturday's game, the MSST backup QB is not a clear answer. Redshirt Freshman Parker Puckett started in place of Taylor against Alabama, but SEC veteran AJ Swann is also a likely option to play. Regardless, I expect the Bulldogs will be less competitive without the SEC TD leader hurling the rock. LSU wins handily at home. I think the Tigers come out with a point to prove and get to work proving it. The receivers have struggled to find consistency all season with catching the ball and Sam Leavitt’s interception numbers are also something that I think could cause LSU to lose. Taylor is one of college football’s best quarterbacks, and if he’s not healthy, LSU’s defensive game plan changes. Meanwhile, the Bulldogs allow the second-most passing yards per game in the SEC, so I expect Lane Kiffin to open up the playbook and attack that weakness. I think the Tigers handle business at home. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 15, 2026 at 2:20 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It looked like LSU was about to dominate the college football world when it beat Clemson 51-10 to start the season. But Lane Kiffin's bunch lost to Ole Miss, came back with a few wins, and then last week got outfoxed by Kentucky in a 35-34 overtime loss. And now there's a problem. LSU is talented enough to beat anyone, but it's one more loss away from realistically being out of the College Football Playoff. That won't be easy with a brutal schedule over the second half of the season. Mississippi State has had two weeks to get over the 56-23 loss to Alabama. It isn't an easy slate, but at 4-1, it'll still be in the mix for big things if it can get out of Baton Rouge with a win. Mississippi State vs LSU: Quick Hits LSU starts a run of three home games in the next four weeks, going to Auburn next before hosting Alabama and Texas. Mississippi State starts its own run of four home games in five weeks after this, hosting Oklahoma before going to Texas. LSU has won three straight in the series ever since the 44-34 loss to open up the 2020 season. That came right after the Tigers' national title season. How To Watch Mississippi State vs LSU Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Mississippi State Will Win The defense will have to step up its game. The Bulldogs have been winning on their amazing offense, but the defense has held its own in key spots. It might be tough to hang with the Tigers blow for blow, so taking the ball away is a must. Mississippi State came up with two takeaways in two of the last three games, and turnovers have been a big issue for LSU, with ten in six games. Why does the defense have to come up big? Why LSU Will Win Mississippi State might be without star quarterback Kamario Taylor. He's trying to get past a leg injury suffered in the Alabama loss, and now he and top running back Fluff Bothwell are questionable at best. There's also the home-field advantage side of this. Ole Miss and Kentucky are good, but LSU should've been better in both road games. At home, the Tigers have been untouchable, winning by a combined score of 194-44 in the four games. Mississippi State vs LSU Prediction, Betting Lines It'll be a different LSU team than the one that walked off the field against Kentucky. It'll be more confident, explosive, and it won't let up – this won't be a back-and-forth fight like it was against the Wildcats. Of course, this changes if Taylor is at 100% for the Bulldogs, but even if he's ready to roll, LSU will be razor-sharp with a much better defensive performance than last week. Can Lane Kiffin and the Tigers bounce back after an embarrassing loss? The pressure is mounting in Baton Rouge as No. 22 LSU (4-2) prepares to host No. 16 Mississippi State (4-2) Saturday afternoon at Tiger Stadium. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. However, the Tigers just surrendered 35 points to Kentucky, raising serious questions about their ability to close out games. Against Mississippi State's explosive offense, LSU cannot afford another inconsistent defensive performance. Mississippi State: Kamario Taylor Is a PROBLEM Jeff Lebby has Mississippi State playing some exciting football, and quarterback Kamario Taylor has emerged as one of the SEC's most dangerous young players. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just four interceptions while completing 66.2% of his passes. However, his availability is a major concern after aggravating a lower-leg injury against Alabama. If Taylor is healthy enough to play, LSU's defense will have its hands full. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has been outstanding, recording 40 receptions for 574 yards and five touchdowns through five games. Running back Fluff Bothwell has also been productive, rushing for 403 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The Bulldogs possess enough offensive firepower to challenge LSU, but their defense remains vulnerable. Mississippi State was allowing 28 points and nearly 380 yards per game through its first five contests. That's a dangerous weakness against a Kiffin-led offense playing at home. How Each Team Wins For LSU, everything starts with protecting the football. Leavitt must avoid costly interceptions and take advantage of Mississippi State's vulnerable secondary. Establishing Jones early should also create opportunities for explosive passing plays. Defensively, LSU needs to pressure Taylor if he plays and prevent Evans from creating big plays downfield. For Mississippi State, the formula revolves around attacking LSU's defense with tempo and forcing Leavitt into mistakes. If Taylor is available, his dual-threat ability could create serious problems. The Bulldogs must also establish Bothwell to prevent LSU from focusing entirely on the passing game. I expect an offensive shootout in Baton Rouge. Mississippi State has enough offensive talent to create problems for LSU, particularly if Taylor is healthy enough to play. However, I believe this is a bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin and the Tigers. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. The Bulldogs will keep things competitive throughout the afternoon, but LSU's home-field advantage and offensive firepower should ultimately make the difference. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. Final Score: No. 22 LSU 38, No. 16 Mississippi State 31 LSU survives a major scare, improves to 5-2, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. He was later downgraded to doubtful on Friday and has since been ruled out. He was shown in street clothes on ESPN's "College GameDay" on Saturday while wearing a boot. The 6-foot-4 quarterback has been one of the breakout players in the SEC through the first six weeks of the season, as he is tied for the third-most touchdown passes in the country (17) and leads the SEC with 290.0 passing yards per game. The hot start for Taylor took a bit of a halt in Week 5 vs. Alabama, as he completed a season-low 55.9% of his passes for 258 yards and three touchdowns while taking five sacks and throwing for two interceptions. Mississippi State and LSU are set for a noon ET kickoff at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge on Saturday, Oct. 17. Here's the latest on Taylor's injury: Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby offered little clarity on the Bulldogs ' quarterback situation Monday, keeping details brief when asked about the position ahead of this week's game against LSU. "Right now, the focus is getting (Taylor) ready to play and then having the ability to continue to create the depth in the room," Lebby said on Monday. "Billy (Puckett) and AJ (Swann) obviously are the two guys that have been competing since Day 1 in fall camp and really last spring. So, those guys obviously have the ability to get work if (Taylor) wasn't ready to roll." The first-year starting quarterback exited the Bulldogs' Week 5 game vs. Alabama in the fourth quarter with an apparent injury. He was seen on the ESPN broadcast first walking into the locker room with members of Mississippi State's medical staff. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs will face off against the Auburn Tigers in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry on Saturday afternoon. The weather forecast calls for a beautiful fall Saturday, where the high in Athens is supposed to be just 67 degrees. The betting forecast is calling for the Dawgs to beat the Tigers by about three touchdowns. This will likely not be a close game, which means we can be a little looser with our bold predictions for it. Here are three bold ones for Kirby Smart and Alex Golesh’s first game in this rivalry: Georgia has a 100-Yard Rusher and Receiver The Dawgs can take advantage of this Auburn defense, which is a bottom half unit in the conference, allowing over 350 yards of total offense per game. Georgia’s offense has been extremely productive, ranking top three in the conference. Georgia having a back and a wideout go for 100 yards in the same game hasn’t happened in 10 years. So, yeah. This is a bold prediction. I think about a guy like Talyn Taylor or Craig Dandridge, who have hit on some explosive passing plays. All it takes is one or two of those and some screens and underneath throws to work for that 100-yard game to come into play. Auburn is also among the worst rushing defenses in the SEC. We saw Dwight Phillips Jr. run for over 100 yards against Alabama on just 17 carries. He, Nate Frazier and Bo Walker have each registered multiple explosive runs. All it takes is for one of them to bust a huge run and that 100-yard mark is well within reach. Dawgs go for 250 On the Ground Auburn is allowing about 150 yards per game on the ground. I think Georgia could go for over 250. They have done it twice already and ran for over 200 yards in two other games. Auburn allowed almost 250 yards to both Tennessee and Florida. Georgia has a better offense than both of those teams. The Dawgs could really blow Auburn out on Saturday, and if they do that then there will be a lot of yards gained on the ground. Partially due to garbage time. Georgia Holds Auburn to Under 300 Total Yards Auburn has possibly the most unique offense that Georgia will see all year. There is an argument to be made that the Dawgs will struggle more in this game than you would initially think because of that. Auburn takes the least amount of time in between plays and runs more options and designed quarterback run plays than any other offense that Georgia will see this year. I am not buying it. Georgia’s defense has been the best in college football. The Dawgs will shut down Auburn on Saturday. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. Final score predictions for Georgia vs. Auburn Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Georgia 30 Auburn 10 After watching the Georgia Bulldogs run all over the SEC's top-ranked rushing defense in Tuscaloosa, Auburn may be in trouble. Truthfully, Georgia is the best team in the country, and Auburn is rebuilding under first-year head coach Alex Golesh. I don't think this team has the explosiveness to score on Georgia, and they certainly don't have the physicality to win the trench battle on either side. Gunner Srockton has also elevated his game this season, making multiple high-leverage throws against Alabama in an extremely tough environment. The Dawgs will roll in this one. This one will likely be over at halftime. The Bulldogs have the talent, physicality, and balance to control both sides of the ball, and I expect them to establish dominance early. Georgia can generate pressure, force mistakes, and turn defensive stops into scoring opportunities, letting the lead grow as the game progresses. This matchup highlights just how dangerous Georgia can be when all three phases click. The Bulldogs pull away comfortably and send another message to the country. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs Tennessee: Alabama -7.5 If last week was any indicator, Tennessee has far more problems than Alabama , despite the Volunteers' win and the Crimson Tide's loss. In George MacIntyre's first start for Josh Heupel, he finished with just a 10.3 QBR in a seven-point win against Arkansas. He'll be starting again against Bama, which is why I like the Tide to cover -9.5 or better . Arkansas lost to its previous three Power Four opponents by an average of 29.3 points, including a 28-point defeat to Georgia — the same team Alabama lost to by just three on the road last week. Tennessee's offense won't be able to keep up with Alabama. Keelon Russell ranks third nationally in QBR (90.0) , and the Tide are top 20 in offensive success rate (50.1%). The Alabama vs. Tennessee rivalry history is full of winning streaks, and this could be the start of another. Alabama vs Tennessee Over/Under pick: Over 50.5 For this Over to hit (I'd take it at 51.5 or better ), Alabama will need to do the bulk of the scoring, and the Tide will push for 31+ points given Russell's recent play. The former five-star recruit has put up an 8 0.9+ QBR in four straight games while accounting for 14 TDs. His dual-threat ability has helped open up the run game, too, with Alabama ranking fourth nationally in rush success rate (53.3%) . That will force Jim Knowles' defense to stay honest instead of solely focusing on protecting the back end. Meanwhile, Tennessee should be able to put up 20+ points to help push the total Over. The Volunteers have one of the best run games in the country (No. 2 in EPA per rush), led by DeSean Bishop . Bishop ranks top 10 nationally in rushing yards after contact (465). Alabama vs Tennessee prop: Alabama team total Over 29.5 Given how loaded Alabama's offense is, I like the Over at 30.5 or better , especially with how the Tide matchup against Tennessee's defense. Even with Ryan Coleman-Williams out, Alabama remains loaded at the skill positions, with eight other players topping 180 yards from scrimmage this season. That includes Lotzeir Brooks , who leads the Tide in yards per route run (2.76). Russell, Brooks, and Co. should take advantage of a Volunteers defense that's 70th nationally in pass success rate (43.9%). Alabama rarely squanders opportunities either, ranking third in the country in points per opportunity (5.27) . Alabama vs Tennessee combo One word describes Tennessee's passing game: rocky. The Volunteers are 128th nationally in pass success rate (33.8) , and MacIntyre has a QBR of 24.7 this season. That won't cut it against an Alabama defense tied for the 14th-most sacks in the country (17). I'm expecting a fast start from Russell after last week's tough loss to Georgia, and once Bama takes the lead, Tennessee isn't equipped to come back with MacIntyre behind center. The Tide, who are ninth nationally on defense in rush success rate (35.4%), should be able to focus on slowing Bishop enough to win by 10+ points. Best Alabama vs Tennessee props Prop pick #1: Keelon Russell Over 240.5 Pass Yards (53.27%) Alabama star sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell should be amped up to bounce back after an underwhelming 16-for-30, 185-yard performance with just one touchdown in the Crimson Tide's loss to Georgia. That said, it came against arguably the best defense in the country. It was Russell's worst performance since throwing for just 188 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Week 2 against Kentucky. Over six games this season, Russell still averages more than this prop at 266.5 passing yards per game. He draws a Tennessee defense that has shut down quarterbacks all season, allowing just 185 passing yards per game. However, what elite quarterback have the Volunteers actually shut down? "Well, they held Arch Manning to just 201 yards." Oh, like that holds up in the year of our Lord 2026. Russell is far better than Manning and has faced far tougher competition this season than what this Volunteers pass defense has seen. Coming off a matchup against one of the country's best defenses, the sophomore should clear 240 passing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 250.5 passing yards. Prop pick #2: DeSean Bishop Over 89.5 Rush Yards (50.74%) With Tennessee's run-heavy offense averaging nearly 43 rushing attempts per game this season, I don't expect that approach to change on Saturday against a very talented Alabama run defense. Over their last three games against Texas, Auburn, and Arkansas, the Volunteers still average 38.33 attempts per game . Tennessee should lean on its leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , to move the ball downfield . Last week against Georgia, this Crimson Tide defense showed some flaws when junior running back Dwight Phillips Jr. rushed for 120 yards on just 17 carries . That's the same number of carries Bishop averages per game this season, and Alabama is coming off a game where it struggled to stop the run. Bishop is averaging 113 yards per game and more than six yards per carry this season. If he gets his usual workload, he should be in a great spot to record 90-plus rushing yards on Saturday. However, Russell has still rushed for Over 25 yards in four of his six games this season . The sophomore quarterback is averaging 7.66 rushing attempts per game, and with the Crimson Tide likely to be leading, as the spread indicates, they'll eventually want to chew some clock. That should give Russell plenty of chances to rack up yards on the ground. The last mobile quarterback Tennessee faced was Auburn's Byrum Brown, who averages 16.2 rushing attempts per game and racked up more than 107 rushing yards against the Volunteers. Russell just needs 25 and should have plenty of opportunities on Saturday. Take this up to 30+ rushing yards. TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 10: Head coach Kalen DeBoer of the Alabama Crimson Tide reacts to a play during the second half of the game against the Georgia Bulldogs at Bryant Denny Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Butch Dill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brent Taylor Sun, October 11, 2026 at 5:39 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After a close loss to Georgia, Alabama didn't drop in the Coaches Poll Rankings , hanging in at number 7. Essentially, Alabama proved they belong with the elite teams, with a resume boasting a win over the suddenly excellent Kentucky and a loss to #1 Georgia that could have gone either way. The Tennessee Volunteers are similarly 5-1, but it took squeaking out tight wins over SEC bottom feeders Arkansas and Auburn. The Vols have generally played well on defense, but their offense has left a LOT to be desired, with QB Faizon Brandon leading an anemic passing attack until he was injured, and backup George MacIntyre not doing any better. So they're sitting put with a #15 ranking. FanDuel's sportsbook has the opening odds set to Alabama holding a -6.5 favorite over Tennessee, with an over/under of 55.5. Week 1 – Beat Furman 56-9 Week 2 – Beat Georgia Tech 45-24 Week 3 – Beat Kennesaw State 42-9 Week 4 – Lost to Texas 17-20 Week 5 – Beat Auburn 24-14 Week 6 – Beat Arkansas 24-17 The Vols are averaging 22 points per game on offense and 17 points per game on defense in SEC play, with the biggest problem being that, for the season, they're averaging only 187 passing yards per game (and that includes their three warm up games to start the season). Running back DeSean Bishop is still carrying the entire offense with 678 rushing yards. Week 1 – Beat East Carolina 48-10 Week 2 – Beat Kentucky 45-17 Week 3 – Beat Florida State 50-36 Week 4 – Beat South Carolina 49-18 Week 5 – Beat Mississippi State 56-23 Week 6 – Lost to Georgia 17-20 The Tide's offense obliterated all of their first five foes, scoring 45+ in every single game despite having only a single cupcake game. Then Georgia happened, and the two elite squads turned the game into a low-possession, high-stakes contest (seriously, there were only 7 combined drives in the entire second half). The Alabama defense has had some struggles this year. They've been a playmaking defense, but they've also given up some downfield passes in almost every game, and then struggled with UGA's rushing attack last week. Still, the held the Dogs to less than half of their usual offensive output. Alabama boasts a much better offense, but the two teams have likely equivalent defenses. However, the game will be at Neyland Stadium. Still, the 6.5 spread with a 55.5 OU has the prediction something like a 31-25 Crimson Tide victory. How the Tide responds to a tough and disappointed loss in their clash with Georgia will be paramount, but I wouldn't be surprised if this one winds up going under the 55.5 points. Something more like a 21-14 kind of game. What do you think? Give us your thoughts in the comments below.

away.headline: Is Josh Ford playing for Alabama vs. Tennessee? TE late addition to Tide's injury report
away.blurb: Three starters have already been ruled out: WR Ryan Coleman-Williams, C Racin Delgatty, and DT Terrance Green. All three were knocked out of the game last week against Georgia and will now miss this weekend in Knoxville. picks.headline: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why?
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Somewhat quietly, one of the bigger games on college football slate this weekend is happening at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium between No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) and No. 13 Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). Both squads enter with one loss and need a win this weekend to maintain a reasonable path to the College Football Playoffs. However, alongside the high-stakes of the matchup are the storylines revolving around each team’s roster. Rebels’ star running back Kewan Lacy will be facing his former team for the first time since leaving Missouri, following his true freshman season in 2024. Meanwhile, former Ole Miss starters Austin Simmons, Cayden Lee and Chris Graves Jr. all return to Oxford for the first time since they entered the transfer portal, following the Rebels’ deep run through last year’s playoffs. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 2:30 p.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss entered the week as six-point home favorites. Ahead of the Rebels' latest pressure-filled matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Sep 26, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Pete Golding looks on after an interception against the Florida Gators during the second half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Welcome to the gauntlet that is the College Football Playoffs….or at least the very real warmup version of it. The loser of this weekend’s game in Oxford isn’t mathematically out of the 12-team race, but it’s going to be a loss that will be immensely hard to overcome looking at Ole Miss’ and Missouri’s schedule. As far as the actual matchup is concerned, going into the game, Missouri has played better on the defensive side of the ball and matches the Rebels’ offensive firepower with Austin Simmons and Jamal Roberts leading the way. The Tigers’ rush attack could have the ability to give the Rebels a long afternoon, and we’ll really find out if Ole Miss improved enough from its nightmare performance defending the run against Florida. Ole Miss doesn’t have to completely shut down Mizzou’s ground game, it more than likely won’t, but if it can limit Roberts and the rest of the production in the backfield, the Rebels should give themselves a real chance at picking up a critical win. In my mind, that’s going to be the key to victory for Ole Miss. I believe this game will come down to the final few possessions and whichever offense has the ball last in that scenario. Given the large sample size we’ve seen of Trinidad Chambliss in those types of situations, I have a hard time picking against those results. Ole Miss 34, Missouri 31 Matt Galatzan All of the talk is going to be about the return of Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee to Oxford, and Kewan Lacy facing off against his former team. However, there needs to be more talk about Missouri's defense, or more specifically, its pass rush. The Tigers have 18 sacks this year, which is tied with Texas for third in the SEC behind LSU and Tennessee. Meanwhile, the Rebels are No. 1 in the SEC in sacks allowed with just five. If the Rebels can protect Trinidad Chambliss and slow down a balanced Missouri offense, they will be in good shape. I think they do both just enough to get the win. Ole Miss 30, Missouri 27 I think Ole Miss will take home a hard-fought victory against former Rebels’ quarterback Austin Simmons, wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. and the rest of the Missouri Tigers. Simmons, Lee and running back Jamal Roberts are likely to give head coach Pete Golding and his defense trouble, leading to a “bend-don’t-break” type of performance, following a bounce-back game against Vanderbilt for the Rebels’ defense. However, I’m comfortable predicting Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, wide receiver Deuce Alexander and running back Kewan Lacy to outplay Simmons, Lee and Roberts and give the Rebels a high-scoring ranked win in Ole Miss’ homecoming game. Ole Miss 38, Missouri 31 Zion Trammell Ole Miss and Missouri feature star-studded quarterbacks in Trinidad Chambliss and Austin Simmons. This has the makings of a high-scoring affair, so whichever quarterback can protect the ball better could decide the outcome. I think Chambliss and Kewan Lacy play their best games of the year, and Ole Miss gets by with a win. Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28 Cooper Ferguson Back in the Vaught, I want to see a great response to the blowout victory in Nashville. All will go well if Trinidad Chambliss plays as he has so far. After a second-half respite in the Vanderbilt game, Kewan Lacy is primed for a breakout game in the 2026 campaign. I fear the talent and connection between Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee, but I do not see the Rebels dropping a game at VHS this season. Published Oct 16, 2026 TYLER KOMIS Bio: Tyler Komis is a beat reporter for Ole Miss On SI. He is a Biletnikoff Award and Lombardi Award voter from New Jersey with more than five years of sports reporting experience. Prior to joining On SI, he previously covered Ole Miss Athletics for 247Sports (2021-2026), chronicling the ascension of the football program and the beginning of its coaching transition to Pete Golding ahead of the 2025-26 College Football Playoffs. You can find Komis on social media channels, including X/Twitter @TylerKomis. Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. Significant implications for the College Football Playoff. Over to Oxford, where either Mizzou or Ole Miss will finish Week 7 in a strong position to make a run in the second half of the 2026 regular season. No. 13-ranked Missouri football will face No. 10/9 Mississippi on Saturday, Oct. 17, in a Week 7 SEC matchup at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Mississippi. Like Eli Drinkwitz ended his midweek press conference, "look forward to seeing you on the SEC Network," with kickoff for the top-15 game set for 2:30 p.m. CT. The Tigers (5-1, 2-1 SEC) have won back-to-back league games over Florida and Texas A&M by multiple touchdowns. Mizzou's only loss so far this year was against the other half of the Egg Bowl, dropping a one-score game to Mississippi State in Starkville. Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1) bounced back from a loss to Florida with a blowout win over Vanderbilt this past Saturday in Nashville, Tennessee. Here's what Mizzou fans need to know about the Rebels, from their starting quarterback to their top playmakers, as well as a score prediction for the Week 7 game: Mizzou has 3 players from Ole Miss CFP roster, including QB Austin Simmons Anyone with a passing interest is aware: Austin Simmons is among three MU players going back to face their former team, along with wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. Simmons' situation is a little different. He's going to duke it out against the quarterback who took his starting job last season. Trinidad Chambliss was one of the stories of the season in 2025, leading Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff semifinals in his first season after transferring up from Division-II Ferris State. But the thing with Cinderella tales in sports … someone has to lose. That was Simmons, who began last year as the Rebels' starter. He's been widely praised in Oxford for how he handled the change and, essentially, a benching. He sustained an ankle injury in Week 2 and never got his job back. All's well that ends well. Simmons has found new life as the starter at Missouri and is beginning to generate some first-round NFL Draft interest. Chambliss is back in college because of an offseason court case that revolved around a medical redshirt during his time at Ferris State. Mizzou has a tough job defending Chambliss, who is currently fourth in the betting odds for the Heisman Trophy. He's mobile, has a tremendous arm and doesn't take too many sacks. Missouri has a dangerous offense, too, with Simmons and Lee leading the group. The winner is rewarded with a clearer path to making the CFP this year. "I wish them a lot of luck," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said Oct. 12, "other than this week when we're playing against them." More: Missouri football's biggest test yet comes in star Trinidad Chambliss More: Why Eli Drinkwitz isn't concerned with Ole Miss' familiarity with Austin Simmons How much does Kewan Lacy elevate Ole Miss offense? Speaking of reunions … Kewan Lacy started his career at Mizzou in 2024. He was a reserve behind Nate Noel and Marcus Carroll. He transferred to Ole Miss after his rookie year, which — talk about sliding doors moments — was among the reasons the Tigers added Ahmad Hardy out of the portal. Hardy and Lacy were Nos. 1 and 2 in the SEC for rushing yards last year, respectively, so the move worked out just fine for all parties. It'll be Lacy vs. Jamal Roberts on Saturday out of the backfield. Roberts currently leads the Power-conferences with 828 rushing yards. Lacy has been dealing with a shoulder injury and missed much of the start of this season. He returned this past Saturday in Ole Miss's win at Vandy with seven carries for 39 yards and a touchdown. Ole Miss's running numbers on the box score are modest, but the analytics paint a much prettier picture. The Rebels' rushing success rate of 60.7% ranks 10th nationally, per Hudl IQ. Every time they run the ball, they're generating 0.16 in 'Expected Points Added,' which is in the top five in the SEC (Missouri's EPA per rush is 0.05). A fully healthy Lacy can only help that cause. He forced 89 missed tackles last season, a number only bested by Hardy. He led the nation with 24 touchdowns. Sep 19, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels running back Kewan Lacy (5) carries the ball against the Louisiana State Tigers during the first quarter at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Ole Miss run defense has struggled So, Ole Miss's offense looks pretty good. The defense, however … The Rebels are allowing 392.4 yards per game, which is the second-most in the SEC. The kicker — Ole Miss is giving up 176.4 yards per game on the ground. That's the worst in the conference by quite some distance. Opponents' rushing success rate against Ole Miss is above 50%, per Hudl IQ, which means offenses are staying on schedule with more than half of their rushing attempts against the Rebels. Only Florida, which Mizzou gashed for 220 yards on the ground, Arkansas and Vanderbilt have defended the run worse in the SEC. Teams are generating runs of 15 or more yards 5.6% of the time against Ole Miss and runs of 30 or more yards 3.1% of the time. The Rebels have given up explosives. Roberts just became the third running back in the SEC in the last 20 years to run for 200 or more yards in back-to-back FBS games. The Tigers are committed to the run game, and unless Ole Miss has found a week-to-week fix, they should find some opportunities for Roberts to get loose. Missouri Tigers running back Jamal Roberts (20) celebrates with offensive lineman Tristan Wilson (73) after scoring against the Texas A&M Aggies during the second half of the game at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium on Oct. 10, 2026. Score prediction: Missouri 41, Ole Miss 38 When I wrote a game-by-game prediction on Aug. 29 before the season, I wrote the following about Mizzou's trip to Ole Miss: "Something about this game just feels like it's going to get weird. Break containment." I have not moved off of that prediction. My chaos radar is going berserk. I am, however, changing who I think will win. Ole Miss does not seem particularly adept at stopping the run. Roberts is not the back you want to see when you're struggling to contain chunk plays. The outside zone and fist fight it creates is not the scheme you want to work out the problems against. Mizzou's defense has been tremendous, but Ole Miss is going to score. The Rebels are too good not to. Our pregame prediction just has Missouri scoring more. away.headline: Missouri Tigers head coach Eli Drinkwitz calls fan message boards a 'cesspool' during Ahmad Hardy update
away.blurb: Despite this, there is no definitive timetable for his return, and even though coach Drinkwitz has repeatedly said as much, the questions still persist at every one of his weekly pressers. Elko even invoked that same "cesspool" phrase when singling them out. The Tigers are off to their fourth consecutive 5-1 start under Drinkwitz, and their head coach is definitely strutting his stuff on the microphone week in and week out. Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz is off to a fantastic first half of the season for 2026. The Tigers are 5-1 and are riding high after dismantling both Florida and Texas A&M at home in back-to-back weeks. Drinkwitz himself has to be feeling pretty good, too, considering his team has done all of this despite missing perhaps their best player in running back Ahmad Hardy. Hardy was a unanimous All-American in 2025, and the expectations were for him to replicate that success this season, but a gunshot wound in May brought all of those ideas to a screeching halt. The standout running back has since recovered and is miraculously working his way back to getting onto the football field. I guess this week in particular was the final straw for the man they call Drink, because the exasperated head coach offered up a final statement on the matter while taking a shot at the very place the rumors about his running back likely started. "I really don't want to have to answer that question every week," a clearly frustrated Drinkwitz explained. "I will tell you all when there’s an update. Contrary to what’s on the cesspool of message boards." Drink isn't even the first coach to fire back at that subset of his own fanbase, as Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko had some comments for the TexAgs message boards after their loss to these very same Missouri Tigers on Saturday. Drinkwitz is known to be a bit of a trash talker , so was this his way of getting one last jab in on A&M before moving on to planning for Ole Miss this weekend? If Mizzou pulls off the win on the road in Oxford, his postgame presser might turn into a vintage WWE promo. It's Drink's world right now, and we are all just living in it.
