away.headline: Ahmad Hardy injury update: Star Missouri football RB not yet back in practice
away.blurb: Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz said that there currently is no change to the Mizzou football running back's injury status during his press availability Tuesday, Oct. 13. Drinkwitz said that Hardy has not yet started a two-week ramp-up period that he needs to see for the running back to return to the field. Drinkwitz, as recently as last Tuesday, said that he'd provide an update as soon as one was available. But rumors began to swirl on various online platforms Monday night, including PowerMizzou at 247Sports and on Reddit, that Hardy may be close to a return to practice. Drinkwitz was again asked about Hardy's current status on Tuesday. The message board poster has become quite popular for a string of Mizzou predictions over the past year, some of which have panned out. "If he practices, I promise, I'll tweet it out. I won't even give it to Pete (ESPN reporter Pete Thamel)," Drinkwitz said. "We'll just do it ourselves. So, again, I think it's going to be really important — I know everybody's excited about where we're at and all that good stuff. When he's available, I promise you we'll be excited to use him. But that's not the story right now. So, nothing new." Mizzou has its idle week after the game against the Rebels. That technically means that if Hardy is able to return to practice sometime this week, he would be in a position to possibly return for Mizzou's next game Oct. 31 at Arkansas. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings One of college football's great rivalries takes center stage on Saturday night when No. 3 Miami welcomes Florida State for their traditional October clash Getty Images Get ready for one of college football's most bitter rivalries when No. 3 Miami welcomes Florida State at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday for their traditional October clash. As usual, the game has ACC and national title race implications , though this season those conversations are focused far more on the Hurricanes, who finished last season as the national runner-up and is currently the heavy favorite to win the ACC in 2026. Things are far different for Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell, who entered the year facing serious job pressure and now risks falling to 3-4 on the season and 1-3 in ACC play if the Seminoles cannot pull a stunning upset. Wins against Miami in 2021, 2022 and 2023 were crucial building blocks of Norvell's eventual ACC Championship run, but now it's Mario Cristobal who has the chance to string together three straight wins in the series after the Hurricanes got the better of Florida State in 2024 and 2025. The return to Miami Gardens also spotlights what has become a notable home-field advantage for Miami in this recent run, as the Hurricanes are 15-1 at home since the start of the 2024 season, including that 36-14 win against the Seminoles in Hard Rock Stadium two years ago. Miami has been absolute rock stars in the ACC and the sport as a whole, continuing the momentum from the team's College Football Playoff run with eye-popping scores and stat-stuffing performances to start the 2026 season. Florida State hopes to provide more resistance than the average Miami opponent, but even that might not be enough to stop the ACC's most potent national title contender. Where to watch Miami vs. Florida State live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 7 p.m. ET Location : Hard Rock Stadium -- Miami Gardens, Florida TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Miami vs. Florida State: Need to know A big stage for Darian Mensah's Heisman Trophy case: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been playing at an elite level all season, but the lopsided wins and predicted blowouts haven't given him the stage and audience that Saturday night's rivalry game will command. Miami may be in a far better place than Florida State this season, but this iconic rivalry will still bring the attention of Heisman Trophy voters to Hard Rock Stadium to see how Mensah performs under the pressure. Currently, he's one of just two FBS quarterbacks with 15-plus passing touchdowns and zero interceptions and boasts the best completion percentage (84.2%) and passer rating (212.2) in all of FBS. Mensah will still have a road trip to Notre Dame and a few other opportunities to shine in the spotlight, but Saturday night could prove to be the launching point for Mensah to push Jeremiah Smith in the Heisman conversation. Florida State struggling against top teams : While Florida State has won three national championships and spent 72 weeks ranked No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll throughout its history, the Seminoles have struggled against the best teams in recent years. As the Seminoles take aim at their rival from the South, they do so staring down a brutal losing streak against top-3 teams from the AP poll. Florida State has lost its last eight games against AP top-three teams, last winning in the BCS National Championship Game against Auburn at the end of the 2013 season. Another losing streak that Florida State can put to bed on Saturday night is a 12-game road losing streak against teams with any AP ranking, which stretches back to a 2016 win at Miami. No one is beating teams like Miami is in 2026 : The Hurricanes enter this annual rivalry checkpoint with one of the most dominant teams in the country, beating opponents by an average of 39.8 points per game. That's the largest points-per-game differential through five games in school history and is currently the largest among all FBS teams. Now, a skeptic would be quick to point out that a 70-point win against Florida A&M will do a lot to juice those averages, but it's the consistency with which Miami has been blitzing its opponents that stands out. Of Miami's five games, only one (a 33-20 win at Wake Forest ) was decided by less than 28 points. Miami vs. Florida State prediction, picks Miami isn't just blowing teams out on the scoreboard this season; it's a team that's also been exceeding oddsmakers' expectations nearly every week. The Hurricanes indeed have the best point differential in FBS (+39.8), but they also rank T-14 nationally with a 4-1 record against the spread and carry the 15th-best cover margin in the country, beating the spread by an average of 7.8 points per game. With those kinds of trends, it's tough to think that Miami is a candidate for an upset alert, and Florida State's road woes make it very possible that this game will get sideways on the Seminoles. Can the struggling Seminoles avoid another embarrassing defeat? One of college football's fiercest rivalries returns as No. 3 Miami (5-0) hosts Florida State (3-3) at Hard Rock Stadium. These two programs couldn't be heading in more different directions. Miami is coming off a dominant 41-13 victory over Clemson and remains firmly in the national championship conversation. Meanwhile, Florida State suffered an embarrassing 44-20 loss to Louisville after blowing an early 14-0 lead. With Miami entering as a heavy favorite, Mike Norvell and the Seminoles could be in serious trouble. Miami: The Hurricanes Look UNSTOPPABLE Mario Cristobal has built one of the most complete teams in college football, and quarterback Darian Mensah is playing like a legitimate Heisman Trophy contender. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards, 15 touchdowns, and zero interceptions this season. Miami is averaging an incredible 49.6 points per game while allowing just 9.8. Freshman sensation Malachi Toney has been nearly impossible to defend, recording 604 receiving yards and six touchdowns. His explosiveness gives Miami a dangerous weapon against a Florida State secondary that has struggled against quality competition. Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. provides another dimension to the offense, and Miami should have opportunities to establish the run against a vulnerable Seminoles defense. Florida State: Mike Norvell Is Running Out of Answers Florida State's season has quickly become a disappointment. The Seminoles allowed an unbelievable 397 rushing yards against Louisville, including 235 yards from Isaac Brown. That's a massive problem against Miami's balanced offense. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has thrown for 1,320 yards, eight touchdowns, and seven interceptions this season. Although Daniels has been dangerous with his legs, his inconsistency as a passer could become a serious issue against Miami's defense. Running back Ousmane Kromah has been productive with 565 rushing yards, but the Seminoles cannot rely entirely on their ground game if Miami builds an early lead. Florida State has enough athleticism to make some plays, but its defensive struggles and offensive turnovers make this an extremely difficult matchup. How Each Team Wins For Miami, the formula is simple: establish the run, protect the football, and allow Mensah to attack Florida State's secondary. Defensively, the Hurricanes must contain Daniels' rushing ability and force him to win from the pocket. For Florida State, everything starts with controlling possession. The Seminoles must establish Kromah, limit Miami's explosive plays, and create turnovers. If Florida State allows this game to become a shootout, it could get ugly quickly. I simply don't see Florida State having enough answers for Miami's offense. Mensah has been outstanding, and I expect him to continue his Heisman-caliber season against a Seminoles defense that just surrendered 44 points to Louisville. Florida State should create a few explosive plays with Daniels and Kromah, especially early, but Miami's defense will eventually take control. I expect the Hurricanes to establish a comfortable halftime lead before completely taking over in the second half. Final Score: No. 3 Miami 45, Florida State 20 Miami remains undefeated, improves to 6-0, and strengthens its national championship case. Sophomore Max Buchanan will be sidelined for an extensive portion of the season. He was injured in the Hurricanes' 41-13 win over Clemson at Death Valley (Memorial Stadium). Despite returning to finish the game, Buchanan underwent surgecal repairs. Given the Hurricanes' cross-training for offensive linemen, head coach Mario Cristobal will have a plethora of options. The big question: Who does he trust the most? It won't be revealed until kickoff, but here are candidates looking to take the starting role, plus a final prediction. After Buchanan initially went down against the Tigers, it was the fellow sophomore who stepped in. Alofaituli lost his starting role at left guard to freshman Max Buchanan. The 21-year-old logged 32 offensive snaps and finished with a 55 pass-protection Pro Football Focus grade. However, Alofaituli didn't allow a sack, pressure, hit, or hurry. He played the entirety of the Hurricanes' nine-play touchdown drive in the fourth quarter, which they exclusively ran the ball. However, Alofaituli doesn't have the traditional size for a guard. He's listed at 6-2 and 298 pounds. It's proven to be a weakness at times and the Seminoles could exploit if Alofaituli is lined up at right guard. It's been a slow freshman campaign for the former elite five-star recruit. Cantwell has logged just 78 offensive snaps through five games. As both starting tackle roles are occupied by veterans Samson Okunlola (left) and Matthew McCoy (right), the only real opportunities for the 18-year-old to play is in the interior. Cantwell has 59 snaps at right guard, but carving out a rotational role has been a different challenge. The Nixa (Mo.) native will very likely play at tackle as early as next season, but right guard is currently up for grabs. Cantwell could seize the moment, unless this final candidate has something to say about it. The Georgia transfer joined the Coral Gables program with experience all over the line of scrimmage, except center. Meriweather has played in a reserve role, but could be the closest to climbing the depth chart. In the Hurricanes' 52-3 win over Central Michigan, he logged 28 snaps and all were at right guard. Meriweather finished with an 83.3 pass-protection PFF grade. Similar to Cantwell, the redshirt junior is naturally a tackle, but he's shown comfortability in playing in the interior. Joining Okunlola, McCoy, and center Ryan Rodriguez at the line of scrimmage is Meriweather, educationally guessed by Roundtable Sports beat writer Anthony Aguirre. He has tremendous and versatile experience, which can benefit the Hurricanes' protection unit. Both programs are powerhouses and multiple National Championship winners, but it's different this time around. The Seminoles have progressively declined since the 2023 13-1 season; meanwhile, the Hurricanes are on the brink of fully reclaiming former glory. Here is what's most important to know before Saturday night's game: Television Channel: ESPN Kickoff Time: 7:00 p.m. E.T. The Hurricanes are -2000 favorites to win and the Seminoles have a +1000 chance to pull off an upset. The spread is at -20.5 and the over/under is at 50.5. The following Hurricanes players are ruled out: Wide receiver Joshua Moore (Upper-Body; Out for Season), running back CharMar "Marty" Brown (Left Leg; Out for Season), cornerback Ja'Boree Antoine (Undisclosed), right guard Max Buchanan (Left Knee), cornerback Romans "OJ" Frederique Jr. (Left Shoulder), and tight end Luka Gilbert (Undisclosed; Out for Season). Junior cornerback Xavier Lucas is set to return from a four-game absence. Star edge rusher Marquise Lightfoot, linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin Jr., and cornerback Damari Brown were banged up ahead of the bye week, but aren't listed on the injury report. The following Seminoles are ruled out: Running back Samuel Singleton Jr., wide receiver Devin Carter, safety Karson Hobbs, linebacker Blake Nichelson, cornerback Jamari Howard, linebacker Izayia Williams, cornerback Jordan Crutchfield, and linebacker Daylen Green. Freshman linebacker Noah LaValle was listed as questionable on the initial injury report, but has been officially ruled out. Meanwhile, edge rusher Darryll Desir and center Paul Bowling are probable. The Seminoles have the second-most rushing attempts in the Atlantic Coast Conference; meanwhile, the Hurricanes have the best run defense in the Football Bowl Subdivision. Sophomore running back Ousmane Kromah is a great offensive threat. He's second in the ACC with 565 rushing yards on 100 carries and scored five touchdowns. Kromah is among the nation's leaders with 38 forced missed tackles. As the Hurricanes' front seven looks to be at full strength, the 20-year-old will meet with swarmers. Seminoles' fifth-year quarterback Ashton Daniels will need to dispute all early narratives this season. He has one of the lowest completion percentages (59.5) among ACC starters. The Hurricanes will likely look to force Daniels to throw more while simultaneously stopping the run – a similar game plan against Clemson and freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds. However, where Daniels lacks in passing, the 22-year-old makes up for on the gound. He leads the ACC with 10 rushing touchdowns. Defensive coordinator Corey Hetherman has a fair amount of experience in facing dual-threat quarterbacks and finding success. The Hurricanes have the highest-scoring offense (averaging 49.6 points) in FBS; meanwhile, the Seminoles have the 20th worst total defense. It should be a lopsided matchup at Hard Rock Stadium, but rivalrly games can get interesting. Miami enters the matchup undefeated at 5-0 overall and 3-0 in ACC play, while Florida State sits at 3-3 and 1-2 in conference action. The Hurricanes are coming off a bye week, while the Seminoles are looking to rebound from a 44-20 loss to Louisville. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. With Miami chasing a potential College Football Playoff appearance and Florida State searching for consistency, this rivalry game carries plenty of importance. Darian Mensah Leads Miami's Offense Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been outstanding during the Hurricanes' undefeated start. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards and 15 touchdowns without an interception, giving head coach Mario Cristobal a highly efficient passing attack. His accuracy and ability to get the ball to Miami's playmakers have helped the Hurricanes become one of the nation's most productive offenses. Wide receiver Malachi Toney has emerged as a major weapon, while Miami's running game gives the offense another way to control games. Running backs Mark Fletcher Jr. and Javian Mallory have combined for 596 rushing yards, helping Miami maintain a balanced attack. Cristobal's team has also been strong defensively, allowing fewer than 10 points per game in ACC competition. That balance has helped Miami establish itself as a serious contender for the conference title. Florida State Needs a Response Florida State enters the rivalry looking for answers after its disappointing loss at Louisville. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has been one of the Seminoles' most dangerous rushing threats, scoring 10 rushing touchdowns through six games. Running back Ousmane Kromah has also been productive, recording 565 rushing yards. Head coach Mike Norvell will need his offense to maintain that rushing production while limiting mistakes against Miami's defense. The Seminoles have shown they can compete with strong opponents, including an early season lead against Alabama, but they have struggled to finish games consistently. Defensively, Florida State must improve its run defense after allowing 397 rushing yards against Louisville. That weakness could be especially concerning against Miami's powerful backfield. A Rivalry With Major Stakes Miami has won the last two meetings between the programs and will look to extend that streak at home. The Hurricanes want to remain undefeated and strengthen their national championship hopes. Florida State needs a complete performance to get its season back on track. With Mensah leading Miami and Daniels providing a dual-threat presence for Florida State, the quarterback matchup will be a key storyline. Saturday night offers Miami another opportunity to make a statement, while Florida State faces a difficult test against its biggest rival.

away.headline: Miami injury report: Is Xavier Lucas playing vs Florida State?
away.blurb: The Miami football team rolled into its off week at a perfect time ahead of today's rivalry showdown with Florida State . A host of key players injured Sept. 18 at Wake Forest and Oct. 3 at Clemson are starting to come back. The final pregame injury report confirmed the return of some important pieces on the defense. The biggest injury issues all year have been on defense as several top cornerbacks, including starters O.J. Frederique and Xavier Lucas, have been out for most of the season. Those problems built up in the Clemson game when leading edge rusher Marquise Lightfoot left in the first half against the Tigers and didn't return. The following players have been ruled out according to the final injury report Saturday: WR Joshua Moore (out for season), RB CharMar Brown (out for season), DB Ja'Boree Antoine, DB O.J. Frederique, OL Max Buchanan, TE Luka Gilbert (out for season). Lucas is set to return to the starting lineup after missing the past four games with an undisclosed injury he suffered in the season opener at Stanford. Heading into Miami's last game Oct. 3 before its bye week, Lucas was listed as questionable until the night before the game, when he was ruled out. If he still can't go today, Bryce Fitzgerald likely remains the starter opposite Ethan O'Connor with additional snaps for Ryan Mack and Camdin Portis, as well. Damari Brown also could start in his place after getting six snaps against Clemson in his own return from injury. If he still can't go today, Bryce Fitzgerald likely remains the starter opposite Ethan O'Connor with additional snaps for Ryan Mack and Camdin Portis, as well. Damari Brown also could start in his place after getting six snaps against Clemson in his own return from injury. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky's offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners' other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners' stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer's primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners' running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . ESPN gives Kentucky a 32.1% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 5-1 under first-year head coach Will Stein after a huge upset over LSU, while Oklahoma is coming off a rivalry win over Texas. Both teams could experience an emotional hangover after their big victories, but I believe Kentucky can overcome that challenge and earn another road win. Despite concerns about linebacker injuries, the Wildcats have a chance to improve to 6-1, become bowl-eligible, and remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. Final Score: Kentucky 31, Oklahoma 20. How do you see this one playing out?

Two teams coming off massive upset victories will collide Saturday night as No. 15 Kentucky (5-1) travels to Norman to face Oklahoma (3-2) in a crucial SEC matchup. Kentucky is coming off a thrilling 35-34 overtime victory over LSU, while Oklahoma stunned Texas 27-24 in the Red River Rivalry. Both programs have plenty to prove, but the biggest question is whether Oklahoma can build on its impressive victory and finally establish some consistency. Kentucky: Can the Wildcats Keep Rolling? Kentucky has been one of the SEC's biggest surprises under first-year head coach Will Stein. Quarterback Kenny Minchey has thrown for 1,394 yards and 11 touchdowns, while running back CJ Baxter has rushed for 484 yards and eight scores. Baxter was outstanding against LSU, rushing for 123 yards and two touchdowns. The Wildcats are averaging nearly 35 points per game, but Oklahoma's defense presents a completely different challenge. Brent Venables has built one of the nation's most physical defensive units, allowing just 17.6 points and approximately 267 yards per game. If Kentucky cannot establish Baxter early, Minchey could face constant pressure throughout the evening. Oklahoma: The Defense Is Carrying This Team Oklahoma's victory over Texas was impressive, but the Sooners still have serious offensive concerns. Quarterback John Mateer has thrown for 1,038 yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Against Texas, Mateer managed just 155 passing yards, and Oklahoma needed a blocked punt touchdown and multiple defensive stops to secure the victory. However, the Sooners' defense has been outstanding. Oklahoma is allowing just 150 passing yards per game, making life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. With Adepoju Adebawore creating pressure up front, the Sooners have the personnel to disrupt Kentucky's offense. If Mateer can avoid turnovers and Oklahoma establishes any consistency running the football, the Sooners should have enough offensive production to win. How Each Team Wins Kentucky must establish Baxter early, protect Minchey, and avoid giving Oklahoma short fields through turnovers. The Wildcats also need to force Mateer into obvious passing situations. For Oklahoma, everything starts defensively. The Sooners must contain Baxter, pressure Minchey, and create opportunities for their offense. Playing in Norman should also provide a significant advantage for Venables' team. I expect Kentucky to keep this game competitive, but Oklahoma's defense will ultimately make the difference. The Wildcats should find some success moving the football, particularly early, but sustaining long drives against this Sooners defense will be extremely difficult. Mateer won't need to deliver a spectacular performance. Instead, Oklahoma will rely on its defense, field position, and a few explosive offensive plays. Expect Kentucky to threaten late before Oklahoma comes up with one final defensive stop. Final Score: Oklahoma 27, No. 15 Kentucky 21 The Sooners build on their Red River victory, improve to 4-2, and keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. LSU might have the best mix of talent, and it certainly has the highest-profile head coach, but it has two losses, and one of them was last week in a 35-34 overtime thriller to Kentucky. It's just assumed that Texas will find its way into the College Football Playoff, and maybe get to the SEC Championship first. But it just lost to an Oklahoma team that pulled off an all-time found-a-way 27-24 win in the Red River Rivalry. The Sooners only have one SEC loss – 41-13 to Georgia – but all of a sudden, the second half of the schedule doesn't seem that bad. Kentucky, because it's in the first year of the Will Stein era, and Oklahoma, because it beat Texas – both programs are in a good place. But the winner of this will still be alive in the SEC, and the other almost certainly won't. Kentucky vs Oklahoma: Quick Hits Oklahoma goes on the road for two of the next three weeks, traveling to Mississippi State, hosting South Carolina, and going to Florida. It's a key stretch for Kentucky with Vanderbilt at home next, followed by a date at Tennessee. The two programs have only met three times. Oklahoma won 29-8 in 1982 and 29-7 in 1980, but Bear Bryant's Kentucky won the 1951 Sugar Bowl. Broadcast Details - TV: SEC Network and ESPN Unlimited (Dave Neal, Cole Cubelic and Tori Petry) - Radio: Sooner Sports Network via 107.7 The Franchise/KOKC 95.3 and 1520 in Oklahoma City, 1430 The Buzz/KMOD 97.5 in Tulsa, and on The Varsity Network app (Toby Rowland, Teddy Lehman, Chris Plank, and Gabe Ikard) What You Need To Know NORMAN, Okla. — Oklahoma gets its first real chance to prove the Texas win was more than one loud night in Dallas. The Sooners host No. 15/17 Kentucky on Saturday at 6:30 p.m. in Norman, and the setup could not be much cleaner for a measuring-stick home opener in SEC play. Oklahoma is 3-2 and 1-1 after knocking off No. 1 Texas on a walk-off field goal. Kentucky is 5-1 and 3-1 after beating No. 10 LSU in overtime. Both teams are coming in hot. Only one of them gets to leave Norman still feeling like the week actually changed something. That is the whole tone of this game. Oklahoma does not need another moral victory. It already got the statement result in the Cotton Bowl. Now the question is whether Brent Venables ' team can stack a second one against a ranked opponent at home, in throwbacks, with the building expecting the version of the Sooners that showed up after halftime in Dallas. The storyline writes itself. Oklahoma just beat the top team in the country. Kentucky just survived LSU 35-34 in overtime for its second straight 35-34 overtime win. Will Stein's group is not sneaking into Norman quietly. This is Kentucky's highest AP ranking since 2022, and the Wildcats are playing with the kind of confidence that makes road environments less intimidating than they used to be. Stein's background adds a little spice too. He was on Texas' staff from 2015 to 2017, then spent the last three years as Oregon's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach while the Ducks made the College Football Playoff. He knows big stages. More importantly for Saturday, he has a quarterback in Kenny Minchey who takes care of the ball, extends plays, and has already shown he can finish tight games. Oklahom a's recent history after Texas also hangs over the night. Since 1999, the Sooners are 25-2 in the game immediately following the Red River rivalry. The only losses in that stretch were to Kansas State in 2014 and South Carolina in 2024. That is a real trend, but trends do not tackle Minchey or cover Kentucky's skill players. Oklahoma still has to earn the next one. If the Sooners are going to control this game, it starts where most of their best football has started all year: on defense. Oklahoma is allowing just 12.8 first downs per game, best in the country. The Sooners also rank among the national leaders in third-down defense, red-zone defense, passing defense, total defense, and sacks. Opponents have scored on only 15 of 62 possessions. The second-half numbers are even tighter. Oklahoma has given up just 27 points after halftime all season, including only three in the third quarter. That profile matters against a quarterback like Minchey. He is efficient, hard to rattle, and dangerous when the pocket breaks down. Oklahoma cannot afford soft edges or impatient linebackers. The formula is the same one that showed up against Texas: keep contain, force longer developing throws, win early downs, and make Kentucky drive the hard way. The Sooners are 11-2 under Venables when they score a defensive touchdown, including 4-0 since the start of last season. They do not need another pick-six Saturday. They do need the same disruptive identity. The personnel is built for it too. All 14 defensive starters began their college careers at Oklahoma. Owen Heinecke has been the tone-setter again, leading the team in tackles in four of five games. Peyton Bowen just took over a rivalry game. Courtland Guillory made the late interception that set up the Texas winner. The front still has Taylor Wein, David Stone, Danny Okoye, and enough depth to keep the pressure coming. If that group plays clean, Oklahoma has a real chance to dictate the night. The uncomfortable truth is that Oklahoma's offense is still looking for consistency even after the biggest win of the season. The Texas game gave the Sooners a blueprint more than a finished product. They scored in all three phases, finally got some second-half juice on the ground through Lloyd Avant, and did just enough in the passing game when the moment arrived. John Mateer did not have to play hero ball. Isaiah Sategna still created the biggest throws on the final drive. Rocky Beers continues to look like one of the smarter portal additions on the roster, ranking among the national leaders in receiving yards per game by a tight end. That is the version Oklahoma needs again. Not perfect. Just complementary. The red-zone efficiency has been solid, and the explosive pass plays are still there. What has lagged is the ability to stay on schedule without leaning so hard on the defense and special teams. Kentucky's defense has not been elite by the numbers, but Venables already made clear that "relief" is not the word inside the building. Every week is still about Oklahoma getting better. The offensive line remains one of the quieter swing factors. Michael Fasusi has been working back from the shoulder injury that knocked him out after the opener, and any step toward getting the line more whole helps the whole operation. Avant gave the run game a pulse against Texas. Xavier Robinson and Tory Blaylock still have to become more reliable pieces if Oklahoma wants drives that do not feel like they are always one negative play from stalling. There are plenty of side notes around the game, and most of them favor the home team if Oklahoma plays like it should. The Sooners are wearing the Bud Wilkinson-era throwbacks again. Memorial Stadium has been a fortress since 1999, with a 153-17 record and a sellout streak that never seems to blink. Venables is 2-2 in conference home openers. The roster has true veteran captains across both sides of the ball. Special teams, once a liability, now look like a genuine strength with Tate Sandell , Grayson Miller, and Doug Deakin's unit playing with confidence. But the schedule context is what keeps this from feeling comfortable. Oklahoma has already seen Michigan, Georgia, and Texas. Still left are Kentucky, Mississippi State, Ole Miss, and Missouri among the ranked or dangerous remaining names. This is not a soft landing after Dallas. It is the next hard one. Kentucky is good enough to punish a flat home team, especially if Minchey gets into a rhythm and Oklahoma's offense stalls early. That is why Saturday matters beyond one week in the standings. The Texas win stopped the spiral and put Oklahoma back in the conversation. A home win over a ranked Kentucky team would make that conversation real. A letdown would turn Dallas back into an isolated highlight instead of the start of a run. The Sooners do not need to look perfect. They need to look intentional. Defend with the same edge that has carried them all year. Run the ball well enough to keep the game clean. Let Mateer manage instead of force. Protect the edges against Minchey. And finish the night like a team that understands the standard is no longer just competing in these games. Oklahoma has the defense. It has the home field. It has the momentum. Kentucky has the confidence of a team that has already won a couple of ugly, important games. Saturday night in Norman should tell us which one is actually building something.

By Cory Nightingale Published: Oct 15, 2026 · 5:07 PM EDT The Inside College Football crew gave its pick earlier this week for the huge SEC matchup on Saturday in Norman between No. 15 Kentucky and Oklahoma. The Wildcats are the ranked team among the 2 teams, coming in at No. 15, but the Sooners have their own momentum going despite being unranked after last week's stunning victory over then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. That means we have 2 teams who'll be coming into the Week 7 primetime clash with some serious good feeling. No. 15 Kentucky is 5-1 overall and on a 4-game winning streak, capped by back-to-back overtime wins over South Carolina and LSU by the exact same 35-34 score. The Cats are 3-1 in the SEC, with their lone conference setback against Alabama in Week 2 feeling like a long time ago. Then there is Oklahoma, which suffered through a 2-2 September that took it from the AP rankings straight out of those rankings. away.headline: Oklahoma vs. Kentucky Injury Report: Sooners offensive line banged up
away.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , following us on Twitter/X , and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. Published Oct 14, 2026 ADAM CARRIKER Adam’s dream of playing for the Huskers came to fruition. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! Will an offensive play-caller change be made after first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer conjured up only 272 total yards from the press box? This is the season for an Oregon team that should be in full rock-and-roll mode at this point, but instead it's been one big, sad trombone of a season. The Ducks are still 3-2 with a not-that-horrible schedule the rest of the way outside of a trip to Ohio State. They lost to UCLA, but they can stay alive in the Big Ten title hunt with one more loss, even if an at-large CFP bid is likely gone with a third defeat and no Big Ten Championship. And they have to do it with Nebraska's former star quarterback, Dylan Raiola – maybe. Nebraska had Indiana cooked, but it turned the stove off too early. The Hoosiers rallied back for a 20-17 win, but that might have been more about the defending national champs not being as good this year than the Huskers being close to fantastic. However, winning in Eugene is still hard, and if Nebraska can do it, it's 6-1 with a favorable schedule – Ohio State comes to Lincoln – and all of a sudden, it's on the fast track to 10-2 – at least – and a possible at-large CFP bid. Nebraska vs Oregon: Quick Hits Oregon ends a good run of home games and goes to Illinois after this. After that, it hosts Northwestern before going to Ohio State. Nebraska starts a run of three road games in four dates, getting a week off before playing Washington, and then it's off to Illinois. The two have never played as Big Ten teams. Oregon won the last meeting 42-35 in 2017. The Huskers are 6-2 overall in the series, with the first win in 1952. The Ducks might have knocked out Bruin quarterback Nico Iamaleava with a knee injury, but they were destroyed offensively with seven turnovers and just 272 yards of total offense. Oregon is a mess. Star quarterback Dante Moore is expected to miss another game after suffering a concussion against USC. Dylan Raiola might get his shot against his former team, but he was beyond awful against UCLA. Brock Thomas doesn't have Raiola's talent, but he got the offense moving in the second half. Nebraska gave up two huge touchdowns against Indiana, but held firm the rest of the way. Oregon's offensive problems won't all of a sudden be fixed this week. The Huskers can force takeaways – three against Michigan State, two against Maryland – but the Ducks are capable of getting their running game moving a bit to take the pressure off the passing game. And about the quarterback situation, yes, Bob Chesney and the UCLA defense pitched a gem last week. But the week before that, Raiola stepped in and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns in a brilliant fill-in performance for Moore against USC. It'll be fantastic against the Nebraska running game, and that will be enough. Oregon is 3-0 when allowing fewer than 140 yards on the ground, and Nebraska managed just 128 against Indiana. This won't be pretty, but it'll be a fascinating late-night battle with a few more points than you might expect. Now the Huskers travel up to Oregon for a 10 p.m. CT matchup, the latest start time for Nebraska since 2014. But other factors in this game make this clash all the more questionable. Dante Moore is out for the game, meaning Dylan Raiola, Brock Thomas or even Akili Smith Jr. will be earning the start. But Raiola is the most poetic option after all and is likely the starter despite a rough outing against UCLA. After going 19-of-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, Raiola only threw 6-of-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions against the Bruins . He also got strip-sacked in the game. Though it was Raiola's only sack, UCLA still brought the pressure throughout. Raiola's main weakness is pressure, which the Bruins exploited last week. Though Raiola can find ways to stay alive in the pocket and deliver big plays, he rarely takes off downfield and has found himself in rough spots. Thomas took over in the fourth quarter for the Ducks and went 11-of-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown. He did, however, fumble on his opening drive but nearly completed the comeback. But even if Thomas starts, it remains to be seen whether he can replicate that success, especially after seeing Raiola's two-game stretch. Now, Nebraska can get to the quarterback, but the concern comes down to the explosive plays. Indiana pulled off multiple explosive plays last week, despite its struggle to produce points and yardage for most of the game. The Ducks can do the same, especially late in the game. Nebraska ran out of steam in the fourth against Indiana at home early in the afternoon. Now, the Huskers face Oregon on the road after dark. The Ducks almost completed their 17-6 comeback against UCLA, so they can find a way to do the same against Nebraska if needed. The Huskers' defense also needs to be cautious with Oregon's rushing game. Though the Ducks don't strike primarily on the ground, Dierre Hill Jr. and Jordon Davison combined for 216 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 54 carries over the last two games, averaging four yards per carry. Though UCLA did suffocate Oregon's run at times, Nebraska could let a play slip by if it's not careful. Oregon's defense also needs to be cautious, seeing how its last two games panned out. The Ducks held USC to 27 points, but Jayden Maiava still threw for 326 yards and two touchdowns on just 23 completions. Oregon also surrendered 205 passing yards on just 13 completions to UCLA, despite holding it to 17 points. Nebraska could do some damage on the run, however. Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker tallied 109 rushing yards earlier this season against the Ducks. Anthony Colandrea could do the same and help the Huskers score. Jamal Rule, Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee all could have moments as well after UCLA's Wayne Knight found some holes in Oregon's defensive line. Knight finished with 103 yards on 22 carries. But this game is also make-or-break for Oregon's postseason hopes, especially with Ohio State and even Northwestern coming up. The Ducks also have a talented roster and, despite their issues, can deliver major blows to opponents when momentum is on their side. Nebraska's issues on the line, in the secondary and even a bit on special teams don't help either. All of this, plus the after-dark setting, provides just enough to tip the scales in the Ducks' favor. Unless Nebraska can truly come out and play like a team that can earn a top-25 spot, this matchup will likely be another so-close-but-so-far loss. away.headline: What we're hearing on Oregon injuries ahead of Nebraska
away.blurb: However, it doesn't appear that things are going to get any easier, with the Nebraska Cornhuskers coming to town, and starting quarterback Dante Moore once again ruled out after the concussion he suffered in Week 4 against the USC Trojans . That will leave either Brock Thomas, Dylan Raiola, or Akili Smith Jr. under center with the start, and a big onus on the offense to show some improvement. While the Big Ten Availability report was released on Wednesday and will again come out on Thursday and Friday nights, we've got some intel on where things stand with each injured player and whether or not they will be able to contribute this weekend. Here's our early look at who we think could potentially be out or limited in this game on Friday night. There was some hope that Dante Moore might be able to give it a go this week after returning to practice following his concussion, but the fact that he was ruled "out" in the first availability report, and not even "questionable," is not a great sign for an expedient return. We will see if Moore is able to go next week against Illinois, but it could still be a couple of weeks before we see No. 5 back on the field, if at all. McClellan has been out for a few weeks now after suffering a broken foot in warmups before the Portland State game, and has been seen wearing a walking boot during games. We will see when he is able to get out of the boot and back to practice, but it might still be several weeks, at the least. "He's going to be done for the foreseeable future. (It's) something he tried to tough out. You know, credit to him. Sometimes you can play through that, but you're probably not going to play as well. But it's one of those ones where it made sense to get it repaired for him." According to head coach Dan Lanning, Platt is still dealing with an undisclosed injury that held him out of the spring game earlier this year. Oregon's coach does not expect him to return to the field anytime soon. "He's gonna be limited for a while with the injury he felt in the spring," Lanning said of Platt. "I don't want to put a timeline on it, but he's going to be out for some time until we see where he's at and continue to progress and challenge himself." After suffering a neck injury during fall camp a year ago, Gresham was held out for the entire 2025 season and has yet to return to the field. Oregon still has him on the roster, but it doesn't sound like he will be back anytime soon. After starting the game against Oklahoma State, Ferguson was forced to the sideline in the first half with a knee injury that Dan Lanning says is expected to hold him out for the remainder of the season. Colorado transfer RB Simeon Price is yet to play this year and has been seen in street clothes wearing a walking boot recently during Oregon games. away.headline: Will Dante Moore play vs. Nebraska? Oregon releases injury report
away.blurb: Dante Moore was listed as out on the team's Big Ten Conference-mandated availability report released Oct. 14. He will miss his second straight game since suffering a concussion in the first half against USC on Sept. 26. Also listed as out for Saturday's game is wide receiver Jeremiah McClellan, who remains sidelined with a broken foot, and safety Aaron Flowers. Lanning said Wednesday that Flowers had shoulder surgery and is out for the "foreseeable future." Flowers started Oregon's first four games and had 17 tackles and one pass deflection. He also didn't play against UCLA last week. "Something he tried to tough out, you know, credit to him," Lanning said. "Sometimes you can play through that, but you're probably not going to play as well. But it's one of those ones where it made sense to get it repaired for him." With Flowers out, Peyton Woodyard started against UCLA and made four tackles. Freshman Devin Jackson also played significant minutes and made two tackles. The one surprise on the availability report was wide receiver Evan Stewart, who is listed as questionable. Stewart leads the team in receptions (27), receiving yards (352) and is tied for the team lead with four touchdown catches. Thursday update: Evan Stewart was downgraded from questionable to doubtful Thursday. Offensive guard Dave Iuli was added to the availability report as probable. Iuli was not on Wednesday's availability report. Friday update: No changes were made to Friday's availability report from the previous day. Stewart remains doubtful and Iuli remains probable. Saturday update: Evan Stewart is officially out against the Huskers. The starting receiver started the week as questionable to play, was downgraded to doubtful on Thursday and is now out. Tony Cumberland – The four-star freshman defensive tackle from Eugene's Willamette High School was injured in an offseason car accident and remains out. "It's a work in progress with him," Oregon defensive line coach Tony Tuioti said Aug. 17. "I don't think it's going to be anything that we'll be able to see him soon. But he's made so much progress. I think the thing that's most important is that we have him with us and just having him in the room brings a smile to all our faces." Trent Ferguson – The junior left guard is out for the season with a knee injury suffered against Oklahoma State Sept. 12 during his first career start. Aaron Flowers – The starting safety is out for "the foreseeable future" after having surgery on his shoulder, Lanning said Wednesday, Oct. 14. home.headline: Oregon Ducks vs. Ohio State Clash Takes Major Turn Amid Julian Sayin Injury
home.blurb: After the win, Buckeyes coach Ryan Day announced Sayin will miss several weeks, meaning he likely won't be available for the Nov. 7 matchup against the Oregon Ducks. Oregon needs to win out to make the College Football Playoff for the third consecutive season, and the Buckeyes are considered the toughest remaining opponent on their schedule. Not having to play against Sayin in a hostile environment could give the Ducks the advantage they need to upset the Buckeyes, especially if starting quarterback Dante Moore returns from concussion protocol. Moore has been out since suffering a concussion in the Ducks' 41-27 win over the No. 19 USC Trojans at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on Sept. 26.
